card.does: Mild hydride. Aldehyde → 1° alcohol, ketone → 2° alcohol.
card.doesNot: Leaves C=C, esters and carboxylic acids alone.

label: LiAlH₄
name: Lithium aluminium hydride (in dry ether or THF)

card.does: Strong hydride. Aldehydes, ketones, acids and esters → alcohols (an ester gives two).
card.doesNot: Needs a separate H₂O workup step. Does not touch isolated C=C.

card.does: Reduces C=C to C–C and aldehyde/ketone C=O to the alcohol.
card.doesNot: Not used for esters or acids in this course.
Leaves C=C alone; does not cleave C–C bonds.

card.does: Cleaves the C–C bond of a vicinal diol; each carbon becomes an aldehyde or ketone.
card.doesNot: Does nothing to an isolated alcohol or a 1,3-diol.

label: NaNO₂ / H₂SO₄
name: Sodium nitrite in sulfuric (or hydrochloric) acid

card.does: Makes HONO; at 0–5 °C converts Ar–NH₂ into the aryl diazonium salt Ar–N₂⁺.
card.doesNot: Not a nitrating agent: it never puts NO₂ on a ring.

card.does: Electrophilic nitration: adds NO₂ to a ring C–H (o/p to OH, NH₂, OR).
card.trap: Looks like NaNO₂ on a tired day. It is not the diazonium route.

card.does: Quenches hydride/Grignard alkoxides to the alcohol (room temp). With heat, converts Ar–N₂⁺ into Ar–OH.
card.doesNot: Does nothing useful before the hydride or Grignard has reacted.

card.does: Acidic workup: protonates alkoxides and carboxylates; opens epoxides at the more substituted carbon when it is the reagent.
card.doesNot: Kills a Grignard or hydride if added too early.

card.does: Strong base: deprotonates an alcohol completely to the alkoxide (step 1 of a Williamson).
card.doesNot: Not a nucleophile and not a reducing agent.

card.does: Perfect SN2 electrophile: methylates alkoxides, phenoxides, thiolates and sulfides.
3° halide: E2 with alkoxides, SN1/E1 with weak nucleophiles.
card.trap: Never the electrophile in a Williamson ether synthesis.

card.does: Lewis acid catalyst for Friedel–Crafts C-acylation and the Fries rearrangement.
card.trap: Not a base. It cannot make an alkoxide for a Williamson synthesis.
Decoy for OsO₄: OsO₄ keeps the C–C bond and gives a syn diol.
Decoy for PCC / HIO₄ / Jones. Not in the toolkit as a selective reagent.
